notes:
**S173-notes.** The continuation proposes studying sheaves, complexes of sheaves, or champs for one fixed partition P, or objects locally constant on its parts. It names derived Hom and Rj_*j^* among the operations under which satisfactory categories should be stable. Under excellence and resolution of singularities, it asserts stability of constructible torsion sheaves with the qualification “sous réserve d’être premiers aux car résiduelles”. It distinguishes that claim from stability for a partition fixed once and for all, for which it says strict equisingularity hypotheses are needed.

The author’s expectation is explicitly qualified: “Je pense néanmoins qu’un [raffinement/affinement] des techniques connues montrera que X admet des stratifications arbitrairement fines”. The text also says “mais peu importe pour notre propos présent…” before beginning an example. Neither this expectation nor the conditional stability assertion was proved or independently checked in this run. The mathematical map context prompted inspection of j:X_i—X; the shaft has a dark tip but no secure separate arrow wings, so the expected arrow remains only an alternative. Hom is underlined, and the two stars in Rj_*j^* keep their observed opposite heights.

This is author page **28**, archive pencil **173**, without a title or date. It is a continuous letter paragraph. Four guided insertions and three cancellations are preserved. The cancelled Pour … di lies below structures vraiment; no caret makes structures itself an insertion. The physical point after constructibles is retained without grammatical interpretation. A separate small dab above/right of the point before En fait is drawn with uncertain origin. At the damaged foot, notre and propos are readable; pour and présent remain doubtful, and no independent cancellation stroke supports H’s struck first word. The accented capital À is visible.
